hypothesis_text: When Gemma 4 26B-A4B agents each independently pick an integer in [0, 100] and the winner is whoever lands closest to 2/3 of the group mean — with the rules stated in the prompt but no strategy name, equilibrium, "beauty contest," or "Keynes" mentioned — the distribution of first-round choices is centered in the bounded-rationality band (roughly 20–40, i.e. the level-1/level-2 best responses), not at the Nash equilibrium of 0 and not uniform/centered near 50.
label: known_good
label_rationale: Sound on its merits: a fully specified game (integer range, 2/3-of-mean winner rule, explicit no-priming condition) with a distributional prediction separating three concrete outcomes (20-40 band vs Nash 0 vs uniform/50), directly measurable. The residual memorization worry is interpretive and rescuable by design (paraphrase probes), not fatal.
